obligation: TSA report of a significant security concern (cyber attack)
citation: 49 CFR 1570.203(a)(1) and (c); Appendix A to part 1570 ("Cyber Attack"); C-TRANSPORTATION-S01
trigger: Compromising, or attempting to compromise or disrupt, the company's information/technology infrastructure. Ransomware on any company system qualifies
deadline: As soon as possible and within 24 hours of initial discovery
notify: TSA Transportation Security Operations Center (TSOC) by the method TSA prescribes (telephone)

obligation: Voluntary early notice to TSA (IC Surface-2025-01)
citation: TSA Information Circular IC Surface-2025-01 (2025-10-25), described in the TSA notice at FR Doc. 2026-17894 (2026-09-01)
trigger: Actual or potential significant cybersecurity incident
deadline: As soon as possible and no more than 12 hours after discovery (recommended, not mandatory)
notify: TSOC by telephone (1-866-655-7023, as published in the notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended for owner/operators not covered by the directives. Company practice: make the 1570.203 call within 12 hours so both are met

obligation: TSA report of unauthorized SSI release
trigger: SSI (TSA-marked documents; security plan portions marked SSI) released to unauthorized persons, for example exfiltrated by the attacker
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if SSI was on an affected system

obligation: RSSM location answer to TSA during the incident
trigger: TSA requests location and shipping information for RSSM cars
deadline: No later than 30 minutes after the request, regardless of the number of cars
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - duty continues during the outage; use the printed RSSM car list and standby laptop

obligation: Report of en route PTC failure or cut-out to the host railroad
trigger: A controlling locomotive on the Class I's PTC segment has a PTC failure or cut-out en route
deadline: As soon as safe and practicable
notify: Designated railroad officer of the host railroad (Class I)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if a company train is on the segment when PTC service is lost

obligation: FRA telephonic report of certain accidents/incidents
trigger: Only if the incident leads to an event in 225.9(a), for example a train accident with damage of $150,000 or more, or a death
deadline: Immediately (as soon as possible after the determination or estimate is made)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a reportable accident/incident results. A cyber attack alone is not reportable under part 225

trigger: Any reportable rail equipment, grade crossing, or injury accident/incident during the incident period
deadline: Within 30 days after the end of the month in which it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a reportable accident/incident results

trigger: A reportable hazmat incident under 171.15(b), for example a release from a PIH car during manual operations
deadline: As soon as practical but no later than 12 hours after the occurrence
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a hazmat incident occurs

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee records, including medical certification data)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Affected Florida residents (current and former employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if employee personal information was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more (possible when former employees' records are included)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor holding company personal information (for example the payroll and HR SaaS) has a breach
deadline: No later than 10 days after the vendor determines the breach
notify: The company (Director of Finance and Administration)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and FBI
citation: No legal duty for this company today
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practical (company practice: same day)
notify: CISA; FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports OFAC mitigation and sector warning

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: TSA rail cyber directive incident report
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a covered railroad
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification (SD Sec. II.C; verified for SD 1580-21-01E and SD Pipeline-2021-01G 2026-10-05); supplemental information within 24 hours of it becoming available
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not covered by 49 CFR 1580.101 and has no TSA designation (P03 section 1.1). Recheck at each renewal

obligation: Proposed TSA surface cyber incident report
deadline: Proposed: no later than 24 hours after identification
applies_at_this_tier: No - proposed rule only; no final rule as of 2026-09-26

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
citation: 6 U.S.C. 681b; proposed 6 CFR part 226 (89 FR 23644); C-TRANSPORTATION-R07
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-26. The proposed rule would likely cover this railroad (P03 section 5)
